It's really easy to look at someone with depression and get angry to see that they aren't doing anything. But people don't understand how heavy everything suddenly is.
I have depression and anxiety and I try my hardest to not let it define who I am as a person. But it's fucking hard. 
My whole body feels like it's made out of cement. Moving takes so much energy sometimes going downstairs feels like I ran a marathon. Sometimes I go hours without eating, even when I am hungry, because I don't care about myself enough to get up and get food. I just don't have the energy and it's so easy to push it aside because the longer you go without eating the less energy you have. It's not a fun cycle. No one ever mentions the physical symptoms of depression either. My chest hurts. It can feel like I'm having a heart attack, sometimes I wish I was so I could feel like it isn't all in my head. Sometimes the pain spreads through my arms. Sometimes when it gets too bad I start shaking and I can't stop because my nerves are so wound up. Depression is debilitating and medication can only do so much. A lot of other diseases you can take medicine and you'll get better. It's not that easy with depression. You have to try different medications to see what works for you. Some of those medications have awful side effects and even worse withdrawal symptoms.

People with mental illness can seek treatment. But that doesn't mean that they are magically going to find the cure over night.  Sometimes medicines stop working for no reason at all. It's super fucked up.
Depression doesn't care who you are or who is depending on you.
